title: `nvs --help` is written for the person reading it, and it names no PHP input
scope:
what a doc comment clap renders may contain, and the removal of `.php` from every input
the CLI names — the four subcommands that never read an extension, and `nvs test`, which does. Not
in scope: which short flags exist, which is [0151](0151.md)'s; what `nvs info` reports, which is
[0065](0065.md)'s; and the lexer's treatment of a `<?php` tag, which is
`rule:statements/nvs-is-the-only-open-tag` and unchanged.
dependsOnText: [0151](0151.md), which made the banner the first thing a user reads.
validatedBy:
`nvs --help`, and every subcommand's `--help`, carrying no `rule:` token, no bare
`§`, no `docs/` path and no `.php`.

summary.headline: The nvs help text is written for the person reading it, and names no PHP input
summary.body:
The argument parser prints a command's doc comment verbatim, so those comments are the program's
output rather than notes about it — and they had been written as notes, citing internal rules
and pointing at documents a user cannot open. Each citation moves into an ordinary comment a
line below, where the project still finds it, and what a user sees now describes the flag. In
the same pass, the commands that never read a file's extension stop advertising a .php input,
and the one that does read it stops taking one.
